KO.rationale: KO is a best-in-class consumer staples franchise with demonstrated pricing power (10% organic revenue growth, 3% volume growth in Q1 2026), industry-leading margins (gross margin 63%, net margin ~26-27%), exceptional ROE (40.4%), and clean cash conversion (OCF/NI ~1.0x). The portfolio pivot to Zero Sugar (+13% volume) and functional beverages is producing tangible results, and FX has turned from headwind to tailwind. Management raised full-year EPS guidance to 8-9% growth. However, the stock is priced for this quality: PE at 27.85x sits at the 89th percentile of its trailing range, P/B at 11.26x at the 97th percentile, and the 3.6% earnings yield falls below the 4.4% 10-year Treasury yield — a negative risk premium. Price appreciation over the past year has been driven primarily by multiple expansion rather than earnings growth, making the re-rating less durable. The $14B IRS tax exposure is a material near-term contingent liability. WTI crude at $108.64 (+76% since Feb) represents a direct input-cost headwind not yet reflected in trailing margins. On balance, excellent franchise quality is offset by near-peak valuation and macro headwinds, leaving a slim margin of safety. The Q1 2026 guidance raise is a modest positive catalyst (pillar 3 bump) but insufficient to overcome the valuation stretch.
